title: Preventive detention in Jammu & Kashmir: what the courts are finding
seo_title: Jammu & Kashmir PSA detentions quashed by High Court, 2026
dek: Jammu and Kashmir's High Court keeps quashing detentions under the Public Safety Act, citing delays and vague police reports. Activist Khurram Parvez spent nearly five years held before his bail was upheld. The administration says its zero-tolerance policy has "established peace".

summary.label: What's happening
summary.text: J&K's High Court keeps quashing preventive detentions under the Public Safety Act, citing unexplained delays and vague police reports.

summary.label: Why it matters
summary.text: Preventive detention skips an ordinary trial; activist Khurram Parvez was held nearly five years before the Supreme Court upheld his bail.

summary.label: What's next
summary.text: Parvez and journalist Irfan Mehraj face trial in Delhi on bail; the administration says its zero-tolerance policy will continue.

story.text: Preventive detention lets the authorities hold a person without an ordinary criminal trial. In Jammu and Kashmir the main law is the Public Safety Act (PSA): a district magistrate orders the detention, usually on police reports. In October 2026 the High Court of J&K and Ladakh stressed that such powers must be used "with exceptional caution and strict adherence to constitutional safeguards", and it has been quashing detention orders it found poorly grounded, citing unexplained delays and vague or contradictory police reports.
story.takeaway: The High Court keeps striking down PSA detentions, citing delays and vague police reports.

story.text: Some cases run for years. Kashmiri rights activist Khurram Parvez was arrested in November 2021 and journalist Irfan Mehraj in 2023, both under the anti-terror law UAPA in a case brought by the National Investigation Agency (NIA). They were freed on bail from a Delhi jail on 22 July 2026; their bail conditions bar them from travelling to Kashmir while they face trial in Delhi. On 30 October 2026 the Supreme Court dismissed the NIA's challenge to Parvez's bail, citing his long incarceration.
story.takeaway: Khurram Parvez was held for nearly five years before the Supreme Court upheld his bail.

story.text: Government jobs are another front. Since 2019 the Lieutenant Governor has used special powers under Article 311 of the Constitution to dismiss more than 80 employees without any departmental inquiry, over alleged links to militancy or separatism, The Hindu reports. In September 2026 the elected government used Article 311 for the first time, to dismiss a teacher accused of raping a student.
story.takeaway: More than 80 government employees have been dismissed without inquiry since 2019.

story.text: In Poonch, near the Line of Control, accountability for civilian deaths is contested. Three civilians died in December 2023 from injuries allegedly received during army interrogation; a senior officer was censured with two years of "severe displeasure". In August 2026 the Armed Forces Tribunal ordered that the action be struck from his record, angering Gujjar community leaders. On 12 October 2026 four cousins were killed by a landmine at the Line of Control: Indian security sources called them infiltrating militants, while relatives across the line say they were civilians repairing a water pipe.
story.takeaway: In Poonch, a censure over three custodial deaths was struck from an officer's record.

story.text: In Ladakh, four people were killed in police firing during protests on 24 September 2025, and 81 people were arrested afterwards. Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk was held under the National Security Act for nearly six months until the order was revoked on 14 March 2026. A year on, he is asking for the judicial inquiry report to be released, a review of cases against protesters and higher compensation for the victims' families.
story.takeaway: Four people died in police firing in Leh in 2025; the inquiry report has not been released.

story.text: On 22 October the Deputy Commissioner of Srinagar appeared in person before the High Court, after Justice Wasim Sadiq Nargal asked him to explain a PSA detention order the judge had prima facie described as passed "recklessly and mechanically", without due application of mind.
On 30 October the Supreme Court dismissed the NIA's challenge to the bail of Khurram Parvez in the UAPA terror-funding case, citing his long incarceration since his arrest in November 2021.

On 31 October the High Court quashed the PSA detention of Umer Hamid Sheikh of Srinagar, ordered on 2 June 2025, and directed his release. It said the unexplained 25-day delay after police sought his detention showed there was "no urgency", and found the police reports relied on vague and contradictory. An earlier PSA order against him, from 2021, had also been quashed in 2023.

On 1 November stones were thrown at a newly opened mosque in Pehroo Sherbagh, Anantnag, during evening prayers, damaging the building and injuring some worshippers, officials said, amid objections from some residents to prayers there. Police registered an FIR, detained four people for questioning and appealed to people not to give the incident a communal colour.

official.text: Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha says a zero-tolerance policy has "established peace", that more than 780 militants have been killed since 2020, that local recruitment has ended and stone-pelting has been eradicated. The NIA challenged Khurram Parvez's bail in a case it describes as terror funding. The army censured a senior officer over the 2023 Poonch deaths; Indian security sources say the four killed at the Line of Control were militants. Police in Anantnag say law and order is normal.
points: Lieutenant Governor Manoj Sinha: "We did not buy peace, we established peace" through a zero-tolerance policy.
He says more than 780 militants have been killed since 2020, local recruitment has ended and stone-pelting has been eradicated.
The NIA challenged Khurram Parvez's bail in what it calls a terror-funding case; the Supreme Court dismissed its plea.
The army censured a senior officer over the 2023 Poonch custodial deaths; the Armed Forces Tribunal later struck the censure from his record.
Indian security sources say the four men killed at the Line of Control on 12 October were infiltrating militants.
Anantnag police say the situation after the mosque attack is normal and under control.

whats_new.text: On 31 Oct the High Court quashed another PSA detention, citing a 25-day unexplained delay and vague police reports; on 30 Oct the Supreme Court upheld Khurram Parvez's bail.
